name: treesum-hidden
description: W1-a (E2, greenfield): treesum — the HIDDEN evaluator. Twelve contracts no arm sees: edge cases, error handling, idempotence, exit codes and one hygiene check that a faithful implementation of docs/requirements.md must have; none of their inputs or expectations appears in the public task text or in the arms' bundle (the hidden windows are 15/25/45/60 s, the arms' 10/20/30 s).

requirements.text: file_sha256 takes a str or a pathlib.Path; a path that does not exist raises FileNotFoundError.
build raises NotADirectoryError for a root that exists and is not a directory, or does not exist.
loads ignores empty and whitespace-only lines, reads a final line without a newline like any other, and raises ValueError on a malformed line.
compare returns added, removed and changed, each a list of paths in ascending order.
build DIR prints the snapshot text, nested paths with / and entries in ascending path order, exit 0.
build DIR -o FILE creates or replaces FILE with nothing on standard output; a FILE inside DIR is not an entry of the snapshot.
verify prints one line per difference in ascending order of path and exits 1 when there is a difference.
Any other use exits 2 with a message on standard error and nothing on standard output.
The delivered tree holds no bytecode cache under the package: treesum/__pycache__ is not an entry of the tree.
requirements.source: baseline/.gitignore (__pycache__/) — hygiene, not a clause of docs/requirements.md; canary finding C-1

contracts.rationale: error handling: a path that does not exist raises FileNotFoundError (1.2); an implementation that catches OSError and returns an empty or placeholder digest fails
error handling: a root that is a file raises; os.walk and Path.rglob over a file silently yield nothing, so an implementation without the check returns {} instead
edge case: a leading empty line, a whitespace-only line and a final line without a newline; a parser that splits on newline and parses every piece fails
error handling: the digest field is not 64 lowercase hex characters; a parser that only splits on two spaces accepts it
every category non-empty, inputs in scrambled key order, two entries per list where order shows: lists must be sorted, an unchanged entry (a.txt) appears nowhere
nested directories two levels deep: relative paths joined with /, lines in plain string order of the whole path (a/b/c.txt before a/m.txt before z.txt), never directory-walk order

idempotence: the same build -o run twice leaves exactly one snapshot in FILE (5.3 replaces the previous content); an implementation that opens FILE in append mode doubles it. exits_files sees the file only: standard output is HC-13's

stdout.text:
changed a.txt
added m.txt
removed z.txt

contracts.rationale: exit code 1 with one changed (a.txt), one added (m.txt) and one removed (z.txt) path: the lines in ascending order of PATH across the three kinds — the path order (a, m, z) interleaves the kinds (changed, added, removed), so output grouped by kind in any order fails
error handling: a FILE that cannot be read is a usage error — exit 2 and nothing on standard output; an uncaught FileNotFoundError gives a traceback and exit 1

end to end, with the snapshot file inside the directory: build excludes it (two lines, not three), verify right after exits 0 (the self-exclusion is applied on both sides), a changed file makes verify exit 1, and the tool leaves the tree's other files untouched

HC-07's sibling: build -o writes to FILE 'with nothing on standard output' (5.3), exit 0; an implementation that prints the text and also writes the file fails here (exits_files cannot see standard output)
hygiene: no bytecode cache is committed under the package (the baseline .gitignore lists __pycache__/; canary finding C-1 saw one in a delivered main). Holds at the baseline and must keep holding
